jurisdiction.name: Uruguay
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Uruguay governs AI mainly through the digital government agency AGESIC, on a legal basis: Law 20.212 of 2023 required a national AI strategy, a report recommending how to regulate AI and regulatory sandboxes for AI and data. The National AI Strategy 2024-2030 replaced the 2020 strategy for digital government, AGESIC delivered its AI regulation recommendations to Parliament in 2024, Decree 285/024 made the governance framework for the AI and data strategies a goal of the Agenda Uruguay Digital 2025, and Decree 276/025 set up the sandboxes. The 2008 data protection law regulates automated decisions, and AGESIC has issued non-binding guidance on algorithmic impact assessments and transparency. There is no general AI law yet. Uruguay is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108) and has signed its Framework Convention on AI.
lead_institutions: Agencia de Gobierno Electrónico y Sociedad de la Información y del Conocimiento (AGESIC)
Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales (URCDP)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 and 13 October 2026 from the official law database (IMPO) and AGESIC's website, and the documents were read against the official texts. Not yet verified from the official text: AI and deepfake bills before Parliament, tracked as leads together with a planned guide on generative AI in the State.

instruments.official_title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial del Uruguay 2024 – 2030
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Uruguay 2024-2030
instruments.issuing_authority: AGESIC; approved by the Public Sector Strategic Committee for Artificial Intelligence and Data
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Public Sector Strategic Committee for AI and Data at its session of 21 November 2024 and announced on AGESIC's page on 22 November 2024. The strategy is the revision of the 2020 AI Strategy for Digital Government required by art. 74 of Law 20.212 and states that it builds on that earlier strategy. A public consultation on the draft was opened in September 2024.
instruments.summary: Uruguay's national AI strategy for 2024-2030, prepared by AGESIC under art. 74 of Law 20.212 with CAF and UNESCO technical cooperation and a participatory process. It sets guiding principles and lines of action in three thematic axes (governance, AI capabilities, sustainable development), covering both the public and private sectors, and defines a process for implementation follow-up, monitoring and a mid-term review.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; replaces the 2020 public-sector AI strategy and frames AI governance, regulation and capacity-building.

instruments.summary: AGESIC's first AI strategy, aimed at promoting and strengthening responsible use of AI in the public administration. It sets nine general principles (purpose, general interest, respect for human rights, transparency, responsibility, ethics, added value, privacy by design, security) and four pillars with objectives and lines of action: AI governance in the public administration, capability development, responsible use, and digital citizenship and AI.

instruments.official_title: Ley N° 20.212 - Aprobación de Rendición de Cuentas y Balance de Ejecución Presupuestal. Ejercicio 2022
instruments.english_title: Law No. 20.212 approving the Accountability Report and Budget Execution Balance for 2022 (arts. 74-75 on artificial intelligence)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 6 November 2023 and published in the Diario Oficial on 17 November 2023 (IMPO). Art. 2: the law applies from 1 January 2024 unless a provision sets another date. Arts. 74 and 75 are regulated by Decree 276/025.
instruments.summary: Omnibus budget-accountability law whose art. 74 gives AGESIC the task of designing a national data and AI strategy for the public and private sectors, founded on equity, non-discrimination, accountability, transparency, audit and safe innovation and on the principles of Law 18.331, with joint action with the URCDP on personal data. It required a report to Parliament within 180 days with recommendations for legal regulation of AI and lets AGESIC issue specific recommendations and oversee compliance. Art. 75 orders the promotion of controlled testing environments (sandboxes) approved by AGESIC on the favourable report of a technical committee including the URCDP.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First statutory basis for AI governance in Uruguay: mandates the AI strategy, the regulation report and AI/data sandboxes.

instruments.official_title: Decreto N° 276/025 - Reglamentación de los arts. 74 y 75 de la Ley 20.212, relativos a la promoción de proyectos innovadores, en especial en el área de uso de datos e inteligencia artificial
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 276/025 regulating arts. 74 and 75 of Law 20.212 on promoting innovative projects, especially in data use and artificial intelligence (regulatory sandboxes and data spaces)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic acting in Council of Ministers
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 2 December 2025 and published in the Diario Oficial on 10 December 2025 (IMPO). The decree states no commencement date, so no effective date is recorded. The Committee had 120 days to adopt its internal rules and the criteria and protocols under art. 5.
instruments.summary: Sets a minimum governance scheme for creating and running controlled testing environments (regulatory sandboxes) and data spaces for innovative projects, especially in data use and AI, and defines an AI system. It creates a Technical Committee for the Evaluation of Controlled Environments chaired by AGESIC with the URCDP, the Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mining and ANII; sandboxes are approved by AGESIC on the Committee's favourable report, may last at most two years, and participants must file a personal-data impact assessment under Decree 64/020 where applicable and an estimate of possible harms and redress. It also provides for financing and declares sandbox activity a promoted activity.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding AI-specific regulation: Uruguay's AI and data regulatory sandbox regime.
metadata_gaps: No commencement clause; effective date not stated.

instruments.official_title: Ley N° 18.331 - Ley de Protección de Datos Personales
instruments.english_title: Law No. 18.331 on Personal Data Protection
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 11 August 2008 and published in the Diario Oficial on 18 August 2008 (IMPO); amended several times (including Laws 19.670 and 20.075) and regulated by Decrees 414/009 and 64/020. The law states no single commencement date, so none is recorded.
instruments.summary: Uruguay's general personal data protection law, which recognises data protection as a human right and creates the Regulatory and Control Unit for Personal Data (URCDP). Art. 16 gives people the right not to be subject to decisions with significant legal effects based on automated processing that evaluates aspects of their personality (work performance, credit, reliability, conduct), to challenge such decisions, and to obtain the evaluation criteria and the program used.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governs training and use of AI on personal data; art. 16 is the main rule on automated decision-making.
metadata_gaps: No single commencement date stated in the consolidated text.

instruments.current_status: Delivered to the Legislative Power on 28 June 2024 (stated on the AGESIC page). Recommendations only; no AI law had been enacted on the basis of it as of October 2026 in the sources reviewed.
instruments.summary: Report delivered by AGESIC to Parliament under art. 74 of Law 20.212 with recommendations for a legal regulation of AI. Built on three orientations (ethical development, protection of human rights, promotion of innovation), it analyses seven thematic lines: institutions and governance, human rights, work and training, intellectual property, civil liability and consumer relations, infrastructure and cybersecurity, and promotion measures, with diagnoses and recommendations for each.

instruments.current_status: Published by AGESIC as a technical guide (page date 18/11/2020; the guide's own publication page also states 18/11/2020). Voluntary tool; still listed among AGESIC's AI resources.
instruments.summary: Questionnaire-based model for an Algorithmic Impact Study that AGESIC offers to analyse automated decision-support systems using machine learning. Aimed at project managers and teams in public bodies, it covers the project, the system, the algorithm and the decision, the impact of the automated decision system, data, and procedural fairness, and recommends a joint session to evaluate the results.

instruments.summary: Recommendations for state and non-state public bodies on transparency and explainability of AI systems, produced under commitment 1.6 of the Fifth National Open Government Action Plan 2021-2024. instruments.english_title: Decree No. 316/024 regulating Decree-Law 15.661 on private tertiary education (art. 43 on artificial intelligence)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic and Ministry of Education and Culture
instruments.current_status: Signed 26 November 2024 and published in the Diario Oficial on 2 December 2024. In force from 10 January 2025 as stated in the recitals of Decree 116/025. Repealed in full by art. 1 of Decree 116/025 (3 June 2025, published 10 June 2025), which restored Decree 104/014; the AI provision was not carried over.
instruments.summary: Regulation of private tertiary and university education whose art. 43 (artificial intelligence) required that AI incorporated in tertiary institutions improve teaching, learning, institutional management or research, and that its uses respect human rights, personal data protection and copyright. The rest of the decree dealt with recognition of institutions and programmes.

instruments.official_title: Decreto N° 285/024 - Aprobación de la revisión intermedia de la "Agenda Uruguay Digital 2025"
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 285/024 approving the mid-term review of the "Agenda Uruguay Digital 2025"
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic acting in Council of Ministers
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 24 October 2024 and published in the Diario Oficial on 7 November 2024 (IMPO). The annex with the revised agenda is printed in the Diario Oficial image and on the Presidency's legal repository; AGESIC monitors and evaluates progress under art. 3.
instruments.summary: Approves the mid-term review of the Agenda Uruguay Digital 2025 (first approved by Decree 134/021) as an annex forming part of the decree, directs the bodies responsible for each commitment to advance the approved goals, and charges AGESIC with monitoring and evaluation. The review adds four goals, among them, under Objective XII on legal certainty for digital transformation, a new goal to set up the institutional and governance framework defined in the participatory drafting of the National AI Strategy and the National Data Strategy, under the principles of equity, non-discrimination, responsibility, accountability, transparency, auditability and safe innovation, respect for human dignity and the democratic system, and personal data protection. AGESIC is the first body named responsible for that goal.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Digital strategy with an AI pillar: the decree makes the governance framework for the national AI and data strategies a formal government commitment and assigns it to AGESIC.
metadata_gaps: The annex text is carried in the Diario Oficial image and the Presidency PDF, not in the IMPO web text.

leads.note: Pending bill known only from secondary sources; parliament search (parlamento.gub.uy) returned HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch, so the file and its status could not be confirmed. 2026-10-22: parlamento.gub.uy pages did not load; no official file located, status unchanged.

leads.title: Proyecto de ley sobre manipulación o generación de imágenes sexuales falsas
leads.english_title: Bill criminalising the manipulation or generation of fake sexual images (deepfakes)
leads.note: Pending bill known only from a party website; status on parlamento.gub.uy not verified (site returned HTTP 403). Issuing act details: Senate (bill by Senator Gabriel Gurméndez), dated 4 July 2025. 2026-10-22: Secondary sources (Lex Mundi AI guide; montevideo.com.uy) identify it as file CRR 691/2025, amending art. 92 of Law 19.580 to criminalise disseminating AI-generated sexual content: approved by the Chamber of Representatives on 17 Dec 2025 and by a Senate committee on 21 Apr 2026. No enacted law found; still pending. Status not verified on parlamento.gub.uy. 2026-10-22: parlamento.gub.uy pages did not load and no promulgated law appears on IMPO; still pending.

leads.title: Ley N° 20.446 - Presupuesto Nacional 2025-2029 (art. 581 y otras partidas sobre inteligencia artificial)
leads.note: Art. 581 funds a Plan Ceibal AI-in-education laboratory and STEM programmes; funding only, no AI governance rules seen. Official text on impo.com.uy/bases/leyes/20446-2025; not read in full this run. 2026-10-22: IMPO text of art. 581 read: it appropriates 200-400 million pesos a year for 2026-2029 to Plan Ceibal for an AI-in-education laboratory and STEM programmes; promulgated 16 December 2025, Diario Oficial 8 January 2026; funding only, so it stays a lead.

leads.title: Informe de evaluación sobre el estado de preparación de la Inteligencia Artificial en Uruguay (Metodología RAM)
leads.english_title: UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) report for Uruguay
leads.note: Presented October 2024; AGESIC page (14/10/2024) links to the report on unesdoc.unesco.org. UNESCO publication, so held as a lead rather than a national record.

leads.title: Observatorio de Inteligencia Artificial en el Estado
leads.english_title: Observatory of Artificial Intelligence in the State
leads.note: Launched 6 September 2024 (AGESIC notice) under Open Government commitment 1.6; an online platform listing public-sector AI use cases, not a document. Candidate transparency register if a founding instrument is found.

leads.title: Comité Estratégico del Sector Público para la Inteligencia Artificial y Datos
leads.english_title: Public Sector Strategic Committee for Artificial Intelligence and Data
leads.note: Created by AGESIC under art. 74 of Law 20.212; AGESIC page lists members and minutes but the founding resolution was not found.

leads.title: Estrategia Nacional de Datos 2030
leads.issuing_authority: AGESIC; approved by the Public Sector Strategic Committee for AI and Data
leads.note: Approved 26 December 2024 (AGESIC page 27/12/2024); data strategy co-created with the AI strategy. No document download found on the page and no AI-specific pillar verified. 2026-10-22: AGESIC now publishes the strategy as a web document (sections including guiding principles) at the URL above; the pages did not load today, so the AI content is still to be read.

leads.title: Relevamiento de casos de uso de aplicación de inteligencia artificial en el Estado
leads.english_title: Survey of AI use cases in the State
leads.note: Survey results report (publication page 30/07/2024); descriptive, not a governance instrument.

leads.title: Guía técnica para el uso de IA generativa en el Estado
leads.english_title: Technical guide for the use of generative AI in the State
leads.note: An AGESIC notice on the AI community of practice (2023) says work began on a first technical guide on generative AI in the State; no published guide found on gub.uy.

leads.title: Joint Statement on AI-Generated Imagery and the Protection of Privacy (Global Privacy Assembly)
leads.english_title: Joint Statement on AI-Generated Imagery and the Protection of Privacy
leads.issuing_authority: Global Privacy Assembly signatories, including the Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales (URCDP)
leads.note: Press (19 May 2026) reports URCDP among 61 data-protection authorities signing a joint statement on non-consensual AI-generated intimate imagery. Multi-authority international statement, not a national instrument; official URCDP or GPA page not located. Possibly a regional/international record if the radar covers DPA joint statements. 2026-10-22: no URCDP page found for the statement.

leads.title: Convenio Marco del Consejo de Europa sobre Inteligencia Artificial y Derechos Humanos, Democracia y Estado de Derecho — firma de Uruguay
leads.english_title: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI — Uruguay signature
leads.issuing_authority: Council of Europe; signed by Uruguay
leads.note: Secondary source (Lex Mundi AI guide) says Uruguay signed on 2 Sep 2025 and Parliament has not ratified. Per protocol §2b this belongs in the regional Council of Europe file with applies_to; confirm on the CoE treaty office signature list before adding Uruguay. 2026-10-22: Uruguay is already listed on the radar's Council of Europe record for the Framework Convention; the lead is kept for the national ratification act, which has not appeared on IMPO.

leads.title: Universidad de la República: principios rectores y hoja de ruta para el uso de la inteligencia artificial
leads.english_title: University of the Republic: guiding principles and roadmap on AI use
leads.issuing_authority: Universidad de la República (Consejo Directivo Central)
leads.note: Press report of principles approved by the public university. Single institution's internal policy, so a lead under the scope test; official Udelar resolution not opened.
